picks.title: Free Tool, Amorph, Builds Custom Plugin Instruments & Effects Based On Your Description
picks.rationale: Free AI plugin that turns a written description into a playable DSP instrument or effect in the DAW, with voice input and MCP hooks for Claude Code or Cursor. Producers can use it right away.
picks.excerpt: Amorph 1.0 is a free macOS/Windows plugin that turns a written description into working DSP code playable in your DAW; its in-plugin AI assistant takes voice input, and coding agents like Claude Code and Cursor connect over MCP.

picks.title: Introducing voice, music, image, and video generation in the ElevenLabs MCP
picks.rationale: Eleven Music generation now runs inside AI-assistant chat workflows through the MCP server. This is a new way to make music, separate from the Music v2.5 story published 09-15.
picks.excerpt: The ElevenLabs MCP server now generates voice, music, images and video from inside the AI assistant you already work in, putting Eleven Music generation into Claude-style chat workflows.

picks.title: YouTube Music gets more conversational with new AI features
picks.rationale: Fresh Made on YouTube launch. 'Ask Music' brings natural-language discovery to a major streaming platform, which changes how listeners find tracks and how artists get surfaced.
picks.excerpt: Announced at Made on YouTube, 'Ask Music' lets YouTube Music users describe what they want to hear in everyday language, alongside a personalized 'Your Podcast Lineup' guide.

picks.title: AI-music guru François Pachet: 'It's no longer the jungle era'
picks.rationale: Flow Machines pioneer François Pachet looks at where AI music-making stands now. It is expert insight on creators and tools, not a business-deal story.
picks.excerpt: Flow Machines pioneer François Pachet (the 2016 'Daddy's Car' Beatles-style AI track at Sony CSL) on how AI-music creation has moved beyond its unregulated 'jungle era'.

picks.title: An LLM Flagged 1,632 Videos. One Was Real.
picks.rationale: A hands-on case study: using an LLM to triage music-copyright claims flagged four of five videos wrongly. This matters to creators hit by false claims and to teams building AI content-ID.
picks.excerpt: A team rebuilt its music-copyright triage and found an LLM reading video content flagged four of five videos wrongly; the only reliable signal was who uploaded the video.
